passage: Examining mid-twentieth-century photographs and oral histories from a mining community in West Virginia, historian Htet J. Aung discovered that Mexican American miners incorporated decorative beadwork and metalwork into their standard-issue safety helmets, creating personalized designs that reflected cultural traditions from their regions of origin. Aung contends that this customization practice demonstrates how these workers maintained cultural identity while adapting to the constraints and safety requirements of industrial labor.
prompt: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.A: To describe a surprising finding that changed a researcher's understanding of how quickly cultural practices among Mexican American miners in mid-twentieth-century West Virginia evolved during the era
choices.B: To summarize the findings of a study that explored factors influencing a cultural practice among Mexican American miners in mid-twentieth-century West Virginia
choices.C: To discuss research that examined the ways in which Mexican American miners in mid-twentieth-century West Virginia used cultural practices to reject mainstream American values
choices.D: To evaluate a scholarly work that provides explanations for the influence of contemporary artistic trends on Mexican American miners in mid-twentieth-century West Virginia

explanation: Choice B is the best answer. The text provides an overview of a scholarly work discussing the cultural practices of Mexican American miners in mid-20th-century West Virginia, and how these practices were influenced by both their cultural heritage and the demands of industrial work.
